chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, both together, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gifted four horses from Yemen to the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). So he [the Prophet] said: "Name them for me." So he [Ali] said: "They are of different types." He said: "So is there a spotted one among them?" So he said: "Yes, among them is a chestnut one with white markings." He said: "Then keep it for me." He said: "And among them are two bay ones with white markings." So he said: "Give them to your two sons." He said: "And the fourth is jet-black with no markings." He said: "Sell it and set aside from its proceeds provision for your family; for the blessing of horses is in those with white markings."

He said: And I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: "We consider the plain/unmarked ones among all animals as undesirable, except for the donkey and the mule. And I dislike the pattern of white markings on the donkey and the variegated mule. And I dislike bright-hoofed markings on the mule, unless there is an extended blaze on its forehead — and even then I do not desire it in any state."

key_terms.أوضاح: White markings on a horse — particularly those on the legs and face — considered auspicious in Arabian horse culture
key_terms.القرح: White markings on the hooves/lower legs of an animal
key_terms.بهيم: A uniformly dark-colored animal with no white markings; considered less auspicious
key_terms.غرة: A white marking on the forehead of a horse — one of the most prized markings in Arabian equine tradition
key_terms.كميت: A bay/dark-reddish horse — a common and prized color in Arabian horse culture
key_terms.وضح: White marking/spot on an animal; horses with white markings are considered more blessed
key_terms.يُمْن: Blessing, auspiciousness, good fortune — the prophetic tradition associates horses bearing white markings with blessing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about horses with white markings and their blessing?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a historical exchange between the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and Imam Ali (AS) regarding four horses gifted from Yemen. The Prophet expressed preference for horses with white markings (awdah), declaring them to be sources of blessing, while directing the unmarked black horse to be sold for household expenses. The second part records Imam al-Ridha's (AS) jurisprudential ruling extending this principle to other animals: plain/unmarked animals are generally undesirable except for donkeys and mules, and even for those, certain types of markings are disliked. This narration belongs to the chapter on the relationship between animals and their riders, touching on Islamic horse-husbandry traditions rooted in prophetic practice.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Bakr Bin Salih, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> gifted to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, four horses from Al-Yemen. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Name these for me<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are of different types’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So is there a spotted one?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is a blonde one with spots’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So keep it for me<sup>saww</sup>’. 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And among these are two yellow ones with spots’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Give these two to your<sup>asws</sup> two sons<sup>asws</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the fourth one is plain and with no spots on it’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Sell it and keep its price for (the expenses of) your<sup>asws</sup> family. But rather, good fortune of the cavalry horse is in the one with the spots’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> dislike the plain ones from the animals, all of these, except for the donkey, and the mule, and dislike the spots in the donkey and the mule being of different colours, and I<sup>asws</sup> dislike the bright-hooves in the mule except it happens to be expanded, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> desire it upon that state’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Bukayr ibn Salih from Sulayman al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following:

“I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent as present to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. It comprised of four horses from Yemen. He (the Messenger of Allah) asked, ‘Describe them for me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘They are of different colors.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) asked, ‘Has anyone of them bright spots?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘There is a blond more toward redness among them which has bright spots on it.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Keep it for me.’ He (the Imam) said there are two blonds more toward yellowness which have bright spots on them.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Give these to your sons.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The fourth one is of one color all over without spots on it.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Sell it for the expenses of your family. The good fortune in horses is in those with bright spots on them.’

I heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘We dislike all animals of one color, all over except donkeys and mules; and I dislike bright-hooved donkeys and mules of many colors. I dislike a white spot on the forehead of a mule unless it has expanded, however, I do not have the desires for it with such condition.’”
